source: Dr. Thaveesak Sangudom, Dr. Theerawut Chutinanthakun, and Wirot Horasart, "Off-season Production Techniques for Pursat Orange (ក្រូចពោធិ៍សាត់ / kroch poursat) in Cambodia," in The Guideline of Climate Change Adaptation in Cambodia (pp. 130-153), Project on Promoting Climate Resilience in Farming Communities of Cambodia, General Department of Agriculture (GDA) Cambodia, Thailand International Cooperation Agency (TICA), and Department of Agriculture (DOA) Thailand, 2017-2020.
text:
Adult fruit-sucking moths pierce ripening citrus fruit and feed on the juice, causing rot and internal decay at the feeding site.

Control approach given in the source (non-spray, cultural + trap-based):
1) Clear away weeds and undergrowth in and around the orchard, since these serve as shelter for the moth during its larval stage.
2) Set up light traps, and use ripe-fruit bait mixed with Carbaryl 85% WP insecticide at 2 g per 1 L water to attract and kill adult moths, rather than spraying the crop directly.
